gap: Locking a pod whose saved operator order has gone stale destroys that order, its note and its saved_at, and says nothing. It is the exact mirror of the defect round 2 closed: that one invented an operator decision nobody made, this one deletes one somebody did make. The path, read in code and not reachable on today's data: break_api_pod.py:419 computes has_operator_order as pod['order']['state'] == 'operator', and a row whose fingerprint has moved reports state 'stale', never 'operator'. So lock() is told there is no operator order to protect, takes the else branch at break_api_pod_order.py:221-237, drops the existing row outright and writes a fresh one with an empty spot_keys and order_source 'file'. The operator's keys, their note and the moment they decided are gone from the register, and the surface shows a lock with no trace that anything was lost. Unlocking afterwards then removes the row entirely, because unlock() drops a file-sourced row, so the pod ends with no record at all of an order an operator genuinely saved. THE FIX is a decision about what a lock means on a stale row, and it needs a state on the payload, which is why it is structural and not mine to close. Three candidate answers, all inside break_api_pod_order.py and break_api_pod.py which P10 owns. Refuse the lock while the order is stale and say so, which is the honest reading of 'finalise' when the surface itself cannot say what would be frozen. Or freeze the file order and KEEP the stale row's spot_keys, saved_at, actor and note in place alongside order_source 'file', so the register still holds the decision that was made and applied() keeps reporting stale. Or write the lock as its own row and never touch an existing one. The second is the smallest and it also fixes the smaller half of the same bug: today a lock on a stale pod is indistinguishable in the register from a lock on a pod nobody ever touched. Pin whichever is chosen in tests/test_p10_pod_verification.py beside the two lock tests already there: save an order, move the pod's fingerprint underneath it, lock, and assert the operator's keys, note and saved_at are still readable through order_store.stored, then unlock and assert the same.

title: Break contents: the pod, its positions, and its arithmetic
summary: The break's contents were a fixed unavailable state on every break in the product, with no input that could ever change it. They are an entity now. The pod is read from the daily traffic file, whose break_start column is the same value for every spot in one break, which is exactly the per-ad break identifier P3's path_forward asked for and which was already on disk. A pod carries its spots with an advertiser, a campaign, a creative, a house number, a declared duration and a position; it states the sum of its spots against its own span with the difference in seconds; it names Last as its own position rather than the fifth ordinal; and it can be reordered and put back.
